description: C++ Polymorphism: Function Overloading, Function Overriding, Virtual Functions and Abstract Classes

questions.questionText: What does polymorphism mean in object-oriented programming?
questions.optionA: One interface or name can represent different forms of behavior
questions.explanation: Polymorphism allows the same interface or function name to exhibit different behavior in different situations.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of compile-time polymorphism in C++?
questions.explanation: Function overloading is resolved at compile time and is therefore an example of compile-time polymorphism.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of runtime polymorphism?
questions.explanation: Virtual functions enable runtime polymorphism through dynamic dispatch.

questions.questionText: What is function overloading?
questions.optionA: Multiple functions with the same name but different parameter lists
questions.explanation: Function overloading allows functions to share a name while having different parameter lists.

questions.questionText: Which of the following can distinguish overloaded functions?
questions.explanation: Overloaded functions can differ in number, types, or order of their parameter types.

questions.questionText: Can functions be overloaded only by changing their return type?
questions.explanation: Return type alone cannot distinguish overloaded functions.

questions.questionText: What is function overriding?
questions.optionA: Defining a derived-class function with the same signature as a base-class virtual function
questions.optionB: Creating two functions with different parameters
questions.explanation: Function overriding occurs when a derived class provides its own implementation of an inherited virtual function with a matching signature.

questions.questionText: Which keyword is used to declare a virtual function in C++?
questions.explanation: The virtual keyword enables dynamic dispatch for a member function.

questions.questionText: Which keyword can be used in a derived class to explicitly indicate that a function overrides a base-class virtual function?
questions.explanation: The override specifier tells the compiler that the derived function is intended to override a virtual base-class function.

questions.questionText: What is dynamic binding?
questions.optionA: Binding a function call to its implementation at runtime
questions.optionB: Binding variables at compile time only
questions.explanation: Dynamic binding determines the appropriate overridden virtual function at runtime.

questions.questionText: What is the output? class A { public: virtual void show() { cout << "A"; } }; class B : public A { public: void show() override { cout << "B"; } }; A* p = new B; p->show();
questions.explanation: Because show() is virtual, the call through the base pointer is dynamically dispatched to B::show().

questions.questionText: What would happen if the show() function in the previous example were not virtual?
questions.optionB: The call through A* would resolve to A::show()
questions.explanation: Without virtual dispatch, a call through a base-class pointer is statically bound to the base-class version.

questions.questionText: What is a pure virtual function?
questions.optionB: A virtual function with a private access specifier
questions.explanation: A pure virtual function is declared by assigning = 0 in its declaration.

questions.questionText: Which declaration represents a pure virtual function?
questions.explanation: The syntax virtual void show() = 0; declares a pure virtual function.

questions.questionText: What is an abstract class in C++?
questions.optionA: A class containing at least one pure virtual function
questions.optionB: A class containing only private members
questions.optionD: A class with only static members
questions.explanation: A class with at least one pure virtual function is abstract.

questions.questionText: Can an object of an abstract class be created directly?
questions.explanation: Abstract classes cannot be instantiated directly.

questions.questionText: Can a pointer or reference of an abstract base class type be declared?
questions.explanation: Pointers and references to an abstract class type can be declared and can refer to objects of concrete derived classes.

questions.questionText: What is the main purpose of a virtual function?
questions.explanation: Virtual functions enable derived-class behavior to be selected through base-class pointers or references at runtime.

questions.questionText: Which feature allows the same function name to behave differently based on the number or type of arguments?
questions.explanation: Function overloading provides multiple versions of a function with different parameter lists.

questions.questionText: What is the output? class Test { public: void show(int x) { cout << "int"; } void show(double x) { cout << "double"; } }; Test t; t.show(5);
questions.explanation: The argument 5 is an int, so the overload taking int is selected.

questions.questionText: What is the output? class Test { public: void show(int x) { cout << "A"; } void show(double x) { cout << "B"; } }; Test t; t.show(5.5);
questions.explanation: The argument 5.5 is a double, so the double overload is selected.

questions.questionText: Which statement about an overriding function is correct?
questions.optionA: It must have a compatible signature with the base virtual function
questions.optionB: It must always have different parameters
questions.optionD: It cannot use the override specifier
questions.explanation: An overriding function must correspond to a virtual base-class function with a compatible signature.

questions.questionText: Which keyword prevents a virtual function from being overridden further in derived classes?
questions.explanation: The final specifier can be used on a virtual function to prevent further overriding.

questions.questionText: Which statement about a virtual destructor is correct?
questions.optionA: It can ensure the derived destructor is called when deleting a derived object through a base pointer
questions.optionD: It is required for every class
questions.explanation: A virtual destructor enables correct destruction through a base-class pointer when the pointer refers to a derived object.

questions.questionText: Which combination correctly represents the two major forms of polymorphism commonly discussed in C++?
questions.explanation: C++ polymorphism is commonly discussed as compile-time polymorphism and runtime polymorphism.
